meta.methodology: Read framework.md, torah_77_packages.json, all reference===77 edges from torahData.js, and the full source text torah_77.txt. For each bechina statement in the source text, verified whether the concept appears as a node in the dataset. Only concepts with explicit bechina language (בְּחִינַת, הַיְנוּ, נִקְרָא) or structurally equivalent formulas were considered. Torah #77 is documented as almost entirely lost ('חָסֵר כָּאן רֻבּוֹ כְּכֻלּוֹ'), so gap analysis is limited to the surviving fragment.

additions.reason: The source text explicitly states: 'וְהַקּוֹל הוּא בְּהַמְשָׁכָה, הוּא בְּחִינַת ו' — the kol (voice/sound, the drawn-out extension of breath into structured sound) IS a bechina of the letter vav. This is a direct bechina statement using the canonical formula 'הוּא בְּחִינַת'. The letter vav is the second letter of the divine Name (י-ה-ו-ה), the elongated connector — identical to its function as the drawling extension of breath into voice. This bechina is structurally parallel to the existing dataset edge (הבל פה ↔ אות ה"א, reference=77) and belongs to the same Torah. However, the node 'קול' is NOT in the current dataset as a Torah #77 node, nor is there an edge קול ↔ אות וא"ו with reference=77. This is a genuine gap. Note: the letter וא"ו itself appears in the dataset as a node in other Torahs (e.g., Torah #1 package 4 — Torah/Makel), but the bechina pair קול ↔ אות וא"ו with reference=77 is absent. If added, it would form a second 2-node component alongside the existing הבל פה ↔ אות ה"א component, both sharing the domain of 'sacred speech letters' within the י-ה-ו-ה Name structure.

concepts_in_source_text_not_in_dataset: קול (as Torah #77 bechina node paired with אות וא"ו)

concepts_examined_and_excluded.reason: The text opens with the statement that all prayer and Torah-study is 'כְּדֵי שֶׁיִּתְגַּלֶּה מַלְכוּתוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ' — in order to reveal God's kingship. This is the framing telos/goal, not a bechina statement. The word 'מלכות' is not assigned a bechina identity via the formula 'בְּחִינַת' in the surviving text. It is the end-goal of an eitza structure (studying/praying → reveals malkhut). Excluded: no explicit bechina language for מלכות in this Torah's surviving fragment.

Lines 2-3 of the source text identify prayer and learning as the activities humans perform, and lines 3-4 describe what they produce. They are not declared to be bechina of each other or of a third concept using bechina-language. They appear in the eitza edge already in the dataset (כשלומד או מתפלל בדחילו ורחימו → נתגלה בחינת י"ה, reference=77, type=eitza). Excluded: eitza relationship, not bechina.

Line 4 states 'כְּשֶׁלּוֹמֵד כָּל הַמַּסֶּכְתָּא, נַעֲשֶׂה מַטְרוֹנִיתָא' — learning a complete tractate creates/becomes the Matronita. While 'נַעֲשֶׂה' could suggest identity, the context is clearly eitza/causal: the act of learning produces the spiritual structure. Furthermore, the phrase 'וְהַהֲלָכוֹת הֵן עָלְמִין דִּילֵהּ' (the laws are her worlds) comes closest to bechina language but is a citation from Tikkunim (external source) being invoked as explanatory background. The Rebbe is explaining the mechanism, not declaring a new bechina within this Torah. Excluded: the surviving fragment does not use explicit בְּחִינַת / הַיְנוּ for מטרוניתא.

The text states 'הַהֲלָכוֹת הֵן עָלְמִין דִּילֵהּ' — the halakhot are her (the Matronita's) worlds. This is quoted from the Introduction to Tikkunim (Patach Eliyahu), not formulated by the Rebbe as a new bechina. It is cited as supporting proof-text for the causal chain. Excluded: citation context, not an independent bechina declaration by the Rebbe within Torah #77.

concepts_examined_and_excluded.concept: יָ"ה (the letters yud-heh revealed through dechilu and rechilu)
concepts_examined_and_excluded.reason: Line 3 states 'נִתְגַּלֶּה בְּחִינַת י"ה' — the bechina of yud-heh is revealed. This appears to be a bechina of something (the state of learning/praying with awe and love), but it is structured as an eitza: 'כְּשֶׁלּוֹמֵד אוֹ מִתְפַּלֵּל בִּדְחִילוּ וּרְחִימוּ, נִתְגַּלֶּה בְּחִינַת י"ה' — when one studies or prays with fear and love, THEN the bechina of yud-heh is revealed. The dataset correctly encodes this as an eitza edge (reference=77, type=eitza). The phrase 'בְּחִינַת י"ה' here names the *result* of the eitza process, not a parallel-identity statement. Excluded: this is an eitza outcome-label, not a symmetric bechina identity.

analysis_notes.critical_caveat: Torah #77 is documented as almost entirely lost. The text explicitly states: 'מְבֹאָר לַמְעַיֵּן שֶׁחָסֵר כָּאן רֻבּוֹ כְּכֻלּוֹ, כִּי עִקַּר הַמְכֻוָּן חָסֵר מִן הַסֵּפֶר' — it is clear to the reader that almost the entirety is missing here, for the main intent is absent from the book. The surviving fragment (5 lines) is a skeletal introduction to what must have been a richly developed teaching on prayer, Torah-study, halakha, the divine Name, and the revelation of malkhut. The gap analysis performed here covers only what survives. The full Torah would almost certainly have contained many more bechina pairs involving: the letters yud-heh-vav-heh and their spiritual-functional meanings, the Matronita/Shechina and her worlds/halakhot, dechilu u-rechilu (fear and love) as modes of engagement, and the revelation of malkhut through human activity. None of these can be safely added as Torah #77 bechinas without the actual lost text.
